title: RDP logon (LogonType 10) as pbeesly on SCRANTON from 172.18.39.2
rationale: F03 records 4624 LogonType 10 for pbeesly on scranton from 172.18.39.2, but with no mstsc.exe, no 4778/4779 and no outbound 3389, assessed as likely interactive/console. Best fit for the observed remote-interactive logon is Remote Desktop Protocol (T1021.001), kept suspicious/low confidence.

title: pbeesly interactive (LogonType 2) sessions on NASHUA following each PsExec network logon
rationale: F28 describes LogonType 2 interactive logons for pbeesly on nashua at 03:11:40, 03:12:46, 03:13:49 and 03:15:03, each within ~20s of a LogonType 3 from 10.0.1.4 and a PSEXESVC start plus python.exe launch, i.e. the -i 2 remote interactive session side effect. Best fit is Remote Desktop Protocol (T1021.001) as remote interactive access, kept suspicious/medium.

title: PsExec over SMB ADMIN$ from SCRANTON to NASHUA with cleartext credentials, repeated 4x
rationale: All five findings describe the same action: pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local repeatedly ran PsExec64.exe against \\NASHUA with -u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by to launch C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe, installing PSEXESVC on nashua. F01/F07/F16/F18 share the same command-line events; F11 explicitly notes the lateral movement is PsExec over SMB rather than removable media. Best fit is SMB/Windows Admin Shares (T1021.002).

title: pbeesly network logons to NEWYORK (DC) from SCRANTON with IPC$ access
rationale: F26 describes six LogonType 3 logons for pbeesly on newyork.dmevals.local, five from 10.0.1.4 (SCRANTON) and one from 10.0.1.6 (NASHUA), with a 5140 IPC$ share access from 10.0.1.4 mirroring the PsExec ADMIN$ pattern. Best fit is SMB/Windows Admin Shares (T1021.002), kept suspicious/medium.

title: WinRM (port 5985) remote shell from SCRANTON to NASHUA for session/process enumeration
rationale: F02 and F12 describe the same WinRM action: powershell.exe as pbeesly on scranton (10.0.1.4) ran Invoke-Command -ComputerName NASHUA, with outbound TCP 5985 connections to 10.0.1.6 and wsmprovhost.exe -Embedding plus LogonType 3 on nashua. Best fit is Windows Remote Management (T1021.006).

title: Attacker tooling on SCRANTON: sdclt/csc payload compilation, hostui.exe and sdelete cleanup
rationale: F31 describes the attacker chain on scranton: sdclt.exe run three times, csc.exe compiling payload DLLs, hostui.exe execution and sdelete64.exe wiping the stager, Draft.Zip and SysinternalsSuite.zip. This is attacker tooling/software deployment on the host that enabled the lateral movement, best fit Software Deployment Tools (T1072).

title: Single NTLM network logon for pbeesly on SCRANTON consistent with PsExec auth
rationale: F19 reports the only NTLM LogonType 3 for pbeesly on scranton (NtLmSsp, NTLM V2) from 172.18.39.2, temporally consistent with the PsExec activity, with no pass-the-hash evidence. Best fit is Pass the Hash (T1550.002) as the alternate-authentication-material hypothesis, kept suspicious/medium.

title: PsExec tool transfer from SCRANTON to NASHUA via ADMIN$ share (PSEXESVC.exe + python.exe dropped)
rationale: not grouped by the consolidation step

title: Tool transfer onto NASHUA: python.exe, Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe written to C:\Windows\Temp and executed
rationale: F27 describes the attacker-written python.exe on nashua writing Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe to C:\Windows\Temp, then spawning powershell/cmd to run Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe for archiving and anti-forensic cleanup. This is tool staging/transfer onto the victim host, best fit Lateral Tool Transfer (T1570).

title: Sysinternals suite downloaded to SCRANTON and accessChk.exe run for permission enumeration
rationale: F29 describes powershell.exe as pbeesly downloading SysinternalsSuite.zip to Downloads, extracting it, and running accesschk.exe from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite at 03:04:34 before the PsExec movement. This is tool staging on the host, best fit Lateral Tool Transfer (T1570), kept suspicious/medium.

title: Steganographic PowerShell loader (monkey.png) on SCRANTON
rationale: F14 describes a PowerShell 4104 script block decoding monkey.png into a byte array and executing it with IEX on scranton. This is obfuscated payload execution on the source host, not lateral movement, so out-of-scope:T1027.

title: PowerShell Invoke-Exfil script on SCRANTON copies archive to remote WebDAV share
rationale: F25 describes a 4104 script block defining Invoke-Exfil that installs 7Zip4Powershell, compresses Downloads into OfficeSupplies.7z with password 'lolol', maps \\192.168.0.4\webdav with hardcoded credentials and Copy-Items the archive there. This is exfiltration over an alternate channel, not lateral movement, so out-of-scope:T1048.

title: Post-access collection and RAR archiving on NASHUA via the remote shell
rationale: F13 describes hands-on collection on nashua: process enumeration, recursive file collection from the user profile, Compress-Archive and Rar.exe archiving into working.zip. This is collection/archive staging, not lateral movement, so out-of-scope:T1560.
